paper.title: Toward Efficient Optimization of Wind Farm Layouts: Utilizing Exact Gradient Information

public_source_audit.resolution: paper equations first, same-benchmark and same-site versioned data second, figure-calibrated deterministic completion last

paper_native_method.decision_variables: two continuous Cartesian coordinates for each fixed turbine
paper_native_method.objective: maximize probability-weighted one-third cubic effective wind speed
paper_native_method.wake: Jensen linear expansion with Gaussian angular modulation and root-sum-square multiple deficits
paper_native_method.constraints: five-diameter pair spacing, coordinate bounds, differentiable polygon/circle land constraints
paper_native_method.optimizer: nonlinear interior-point method with exact objective and constraint gradients and BFGS Hessian updates
paper_native_method.initialization: uniform staggered layout, one random Latin-hypercube layout, five random starts or twenty random starts
paper_native_method.declared_solver_completion: pure C++ feasible averaged log-barrier continuation with exact first derivatives, limited-memory BFGS and Armijo backtracking

classical.turbine: 40 m diameter, 60 m hub, roughness 0.3 m, spacing 200 m
classical.wind_case_3: 36 directions and 8, 12 and 17 m/s with figure-only joint probabilities

scaling.turbine: Vestas V80 2 MW dimensional lineage, 80 m diameter, 70 m hub, spacing 400 m
scaling.wind: Figure-5 Horns Rev directional frequencies at stated average 10 m/s

land.copenhagen: 37 turbines, 2500 by 5000 m displayed domain, 66.2 percent feasible figure-derived polygon, Horns Rev wind
land.ring: 20 turbines in a 50 m annulus represented by 750 and 800 m radii, north wind at 10 m/s

missing_information: numeric Figure-5 Horns Rev array and direction convention
Copenhagen boundary vertices and forbidden-zone partitions
exact ring radii beyond the stated 50 m width and plotted dimensions
V80 hub and surface roughness values consumed by the authors
author layouts, gradients, convergence histories and timing environment
conflicts_and_completions: Use the versioned T05 same-classical-benchmark Figure digitization for Case 3 and retain a distinct T08 semantic identity.
Use T25 public Horns Rev directional frequencies, rotate from wind-from to the T08 plotted wind-to convention, normalize and apply the paper-stated 10 m/s.

Use V80 diameter 80 m and hub 70 m; retain 0.3 m because it is the paper's sole numerical roughness and Sections 4.2-4.3 do not state a replacement. This is a declared nearest-paper completion, not an asserted V80 site fact.
Digitize Fig. 9 Copenhagen vertices and horizontally affine-calibrate polygon area to exactly 66.2 percent; use signed distance because the paper does not publish dynamic partitions.
Use visible ring centre 1000/1000 m and radii 750/800 m, preserving the stated 50 m width.
Map deterministic Latin-hypercube ranks to a strictly feasible staggered lattice, since the paper does not state how infeasible random starts are admitted.
Interpret Section 4.3 random results as five-start roles while preserving the figures as qualitative one-random-layout evidence.

paper_protocol.derivation: nine classical problems times USL, 5S and 20S; nine scaling problems times USL and RSL; two land problems times USL and 5S
paper_protocol.repeats: ten independent repeats for every classical 5S and 20S role; deterministic or single displayed roles once
paper_protocol.target_only_boundary: GA, HGA and finite-difference diagnostics are paper comparators, not target contribution implementations

formal_budgets.interpretation: complete objective-plus-exact-gradient physical evaluations, selected to cover the paper-reported exact-gradient work ranges without claiming MATLAB iteration identity

hpc.objective_kernel: one shared traversal computes efficiency and exact coordinate gradient; fixed wind-state/turbine tasks and deterministic chunk reduction
hpc.constraint_kernel: O(N squared) pair constraints use a measured serial fast path below 20000 pairs and retain a deterministic parallel path for larger extensions
hpc.single_start: all cores parallelize the objective; lightweight constraints remain serial after measured admission
hpc.multi_start: fixed worker groups divide all visible cores across 5 or 20 independent barrier solves without nested oversubscription
hpc.required_invariant: one-worker and all-worker objective, gradient, final layout, feasibility and scientific hash identity

physical_fes_definition: one complete probability-weighted layout objective and simultaneous exact-gradient evaluation; constraint/barrier arithmetic is reported separately
claim_boundary: Flexible equation-level academic reproduction of every paper problem and proposed IPM role; not author MATLAB/fmincon source, exact wind or land arrays, partition, random stream, optimizer trajectory, numerical table/timing replay or first parallelization claim.
